headline: Keeps the federal government funded through December 11, 2026, and extends many expiring programs, including veterans, highway, and trade programs.
what_it_does: This law funds most federal agencies at their 2026 levels through December 11, 2026, or until regular 2027 spending bills pass, which prevents a government shutdown on October 1, 2026. Some programs, such as WIC, Small Business Administration loans, disaster relief, the Indian Health Service, and wildfire fighting, get extra money or flexibility. It also extends many expiring programs, mostly through December 11, 2026, and extends duty-free trade benefits for sub-Saharan Africa and Haiti through 2028.

who_it_affects.group: Federal employees and people who use federal services
who_it_affects.how: Agencies stay funded and open through December 11, 2026, instead of shutting down when the new budget year starts October 1.

who_it_affects.group: Mothers, babies, and young children in the WIC nutrition program
who_it_affects.how: WIC is one of the programs that gets extra funding or flexibility under the temporary spending.

who_it_affects.group: Homeless veterans and very low-income veteran families
who_it_affects.how: VA housing help, outreach, treatment, and support service programs continue through December 11, 2026.
Nursing home care, rural ambulance payments, help adapting homes, and adaptive sports programs continue through December 11, 2026.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans and organizations focused on suicide prevention and mental health
who_it_affects.how: Community suicide prevention grants, the rural mental health program, and mental health support for family caregivers continue through December 11, 2026.

who_it_affects.group: Veterans using GI Bill education benefits
who_it_affects.how: Students whose school or program closed keep protection for their education benefits through December 11, 2026.

who_it_affects.group: States and local governments that build roads and run transit
who_it_affects.how: Federal highway, transit, and road safety programs continue through December 11, 2026, and the deadline to use certain past highway grant funds moves to September 30, 2027.

who_it_affects.group: Importers and businesses that trade with sub-Saharan Africa and Haiti
who_it_affects.how: Duty-free access to the U.S. market for eligible goods, including clothing, is extended through December 31, 2028.

who_it_affects.group: Businesses that import goods into the U.S.
who_it_affects.how: Certain customs user fees, including merchandise processing fees, are extended through March 31, 2032.

who_it_affects.group: Hemp farmers and hemp product businesses
who_it_affects.how: Parts of the new legal definition of hemp are delayed until December 11, 2026.

who_it_affects.group: Residents of the Northern Mariana Islands
who_it_affects.how: The territory gets more Medicaid funding for 2026.
Federal grain inspection fees and related programs continue through December 11, 2026.
The State Department can keep collecting certain passport fees through December 11, 2026.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted September 2, 2026. Most funding and extensions last through December 11, 2026. Trade benefits run through December 31, 2028, and customs fees through March 31, 2032.
